Galette des Rois

Served at: Epiphany (Three Kings Day)

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 40-45 min

The Galette des Rois, or 'King's Cake,' is a beloved French tradition enjoyed throughout January to celebrate Epiphany, or Three Kings Day. This flaky puff pastry cake, filled with a rich almond cream (frangipane), conceals a small charm called a 'fève,' and whoever finds it is crowned king or queen for the day, bringing good fortune.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (100 g) almond flour
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) almond extract (or 1 tablespoon / 15 ml dark rum)
  • Pinch of salt
  • 2 sheets (from a 14-ounce / 400 g package) store-bought puff pastry, thawed
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) water or milk
  • 1 fève (small ceramic charm or a whole almond)

Method

  1. In a medium bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
  2. Beat in the 2 large eggs one at a time, ensuring each is fully incorporated before adding the next.
  3. Stir in the almond flour, almond extract (or rum), and a pinch of salt until just combined to form the frangipane filling.
  4. Lightly flour a clean surface and roll out each puff pastry sheet slightly to about a 10-inch (25 cm) circle.
  5. Place one pastry circle on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
  6. Spread the frangipane mixture evenly over the pastry circle, leaving a 1-inch (2.5 cm) border around the edge.
  7. Carefully place the fève somewhere within the frangipane, ensuring it's fully covered.
  8. Lightly moisten the exposed pastry border with a little water.
  9. Place the second pastry circle directly on top of the first, aligning the edges.
  10. Press down firmly around the edges to seal the two pastry circles together, then crimp with a fork for a decorative finish.
  11. In a small bowl, whisk the egg yolk with 1 tablespoon (15 ml) of water or milk to create an egg wash.
  12. Brush the top of the galette generously with the egg wash, being careful not to let it drip down the sides (this can prevent the pastry from rising).
  13. Using the tip of a sharp knife, gently score a decorative pattern onto the top of the galette, such as spirals or a sunburst, without cutting through the pastry.
  14. Chill the galette in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to firm up the pastry and frangipane.
  15. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  16. Bake for 30 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 350°F (175°C) and continue baking for another 10-15 minutes, or until the galette is deeply golden brown and puffed.
  17. Let the galette cool on the baking sheet for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing and serving warm.

Tips

  • For an extra shine, you can brush the warm galette with a thin layer of apricot jam (warmed and strained) immediately after it comes out of the oven.
  • Ensure your puff pastry is very cold before baking; this helps achieve maximum puff and flakiness.
  • Traditionally, the youngest person at the table sits under the table and calls out who receives each slice, ensuring fairness in finding the fève.
